title: add edge-rag-lite quickstart and mobile tooling for local retriever + tool-calling
author: Priya Khatri
description: Motivation: provide a compact, opinionated RAG quickstart aimed at mobile and edge clients that cannot rely on a hosted vector store or heavy dependencies. This PR introduces an "edge-rag-lite" example and a small helper library that demonstrates: 1) local SQLite-backed dense vector store (using sqlite + vectorkit shim), 2) on-device embedding adapter (pluggable; example uses an emulated lightweight embedder for CI), 3) a tool-calling pattern for mobile capabilities (camera, local search, external http) with explicit safety gating, 4) an async streaming flow that preserves Redwood-style streaming semantics, and 5) CI run that verifies the quickstart end-to-end in an emulator. What changed: added a new example directory examples/edge-rag-lite with a multi-file quickstart (README.md, example app in TypeScript, small Go-based local retriever shim for native builds, Dockerfile for emulator CI). Also added a focused docs site fragment to quickstarts/index that links to the new guide and a short migration note for teams using the hosted retriever. The README is written as a step-by-step tutorial (install, run local retriever, run mock embedding service, run the example client, test tool-calls) and includes troubleshooting tips for common permission errors on mobile emulators. Checklist: - [x] example app with runnable scripts (yarn start-emulator, make run-retriever) - [x] README that doubles as tutorial text for docs site fragment - [x] minimal helper library (edge-rag-lite) published as local package in examples monorepo (not yet on npm) - [x] CI workflow that runs unit tests and a headless emulator smoke test - [x] documentation cross-links to quickstarts index and SDKs Motivation/context: many customers want RAG on-device or in constrained deployments (air-gapped field devices, mobile apps that need offline fallback). This PR provides a reproducible pattern and clear tradeoffs around freshness, retrieval latency, and embedding quality. Usage notes: the example intentionally uses a small in-memory embedding fallback to keep the quickstart self-contained; production users should replace the embedder with a quantized lightweight model or a secure remote embedding endpoint. Security: tool-calling hooks are gated by a simple permission layer in the example (user prompts + allowlist). The README calls out the need to integrate platform UI prompts and consent flows in real apps. Migration notes: teams using hosted retrievers can follow the README section "Hosted -> Edge migration" to shrink payloads and adapt caching policies. Related: opens a follow-up proposed RFC in ENG-4032 for a unified edge retriever API. Links: quickstart page will live at /docs/quickstarts/edge-rag-lite after site deploy. This description includes steps and rationale but omits large diffs; changed files show the exact surface area below.

merge_commit_message: Add edge-rag-lite quickstart and mobile tooling (Priya Khatri) — introduces local sqlite retriever shim, TS client example, docs fragment, and CI emulator smoke tests
release_notes: Added 'Edge RAG (lightweight)' quickstart: a self-contained example showing how to run a SQLite-backed retriever and tool-calling pattern for mobile/edge clients. Useful for teams needing offline or air-gapped retrieval patterns; not intended as a production datastore. See docs/quickstarts/edge-rag-lite for migration guidance and tradeoffs.
notes_for_maintainers: This example ships a small C-bindings sqlite binary for CI convenience; maintainers should ensure the CI cache policy keeps binaries under allowed storage. The helper library lives under examples/edge-rag-lite/edge-rag-lite-lib and is intentionally minimal — do not publish to central registries without security review. Follow-up: RFC ENG-4032 will propose a shared edge retriever interface across SDKs.
risk_assessment: Low: example lives under examples/ and docs/ only, CI adds small emulator job. No production code changes to runtime. Ensure security review before extracting helper lib for production use.
